must_fix.issue: Repeated end-of-section closer. A version of 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms ... in writing' ends the Elounda, Agios Nikolaos, Heraklion coast, Rethymno and west sections, on top of the house-rules paragraph and the closing section. Four of five readers called it a template, a sales script or a sales loop, and the sceptic said it makes the blanks look as if they were left there to sell the advisor.
must_fix.fix: Keep the Advisor line in two places only: the house-rules paragraph in 'How to compare Crete venues like for like' ('Your Wedded Advisor asks each venue on your shortlist and confirms these in writing for your date: the curfew, minimum nights, music rules, set-up and pack-down times, and the rain plan for every outdoor space.') and the closing section. Delete these lines entirely: 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms capacity, exclusive use, curfew and minimum nights in writing for any Elounda venue on your shortlist.'; 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms capacity, exclusive use, curfew and minimum nights in writing for any venue on this coast.'; 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms room counts, ceremony options, exclusive use and curfew in writing for every venue in the west.' Replace 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms capacity, exclusive use and curfew in writing for St. Nicolas Bay, Minos Beach and Minos Palace before you shortlist them for a large group.' with 'Ask St. Nicolas Bay, Minos Beach and Minos Palace for a written capacity before you shortlist them for a large group.' Under Caramel, cut the second sentence so the paragraph reads only 'If you want a legal ceremony as well, ask Caramel whether one can be held on site, or plan a civil ceremony separately.' Let each area end on its last venue fact. Add no new facts.

should_fix.issue: The Entry/Exit System paragraph sits under 'Transfers for guests', so the heading does not match what is under it. Readers came for coaches and drive times and got border control first; the search visitor said a mismatched heading makes her stop trusting the headings.
should_fix.fix: Move the paragraph 'Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay now have fingerprints and a photo taken under the European Entry/Exit System. It is free and needs nothing done before arrival, but border crossings can be slow, so allow plenty of time for connections.' (with its fact_206 comment) out of '### Transfers for guests' and place it directly after 'The airport your guests land at in Crete shapes the whole trip, so settle it before anyone books a flight.' at the top of '## Getting to Crete for your wedding'. 'Transfers for guests' then opens with 'In peak season, traffic on the islands can be heavily congested.' Wording unchanged.

should_fix.issue: The legal section is hard to follow. The planner couple cannot tell whether they must be at the Registry Office registration within 40 days or whether it happens after they fly home, and the funding parent had to read the CNI paragraph twice.
should_fix.fix: Registration, only as the sources support (fact_16 says the Elounda Peninsula civil package includes a round-trip transfer to the Registry Office; fact_02 says the Elounda Beach package includes an escorted transfer to the authorities to register the marriage; neither says whether the couple must attend). Replace 'It states that the marriage must then be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days. <!-- fact_16 --> Keep a weekday free in the itinerary.' with 'It states that the marriage must then be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days, and its civil package includes a round trip to the Registry Office. <!-- fact_16 --> Ask your venue whether you need to be there in person, and keep a weekday free in the itinerary until you know.' CNI paragraph: split 'DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so ask whether you need one, where to get it, and whether it needs an apostille.' into 'DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia. Some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so ask three things: whether you need one, where to get it, and whether it needs an apostille.' Write out 'Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)' on first use. Do not say who prepares or lodges the paperwork, and do not imply Wedded Wonderland helps with legal, church or religious paperwork.

should_fix.issue: Per-venue 'Not published' lists run to four or five items, and with the six-column table the page keeps landing on what is missing rather than what each venue offers. Phone and iPad readers also have to swipe the table sideways.
should_fix.fix: Keep every 'Not published' line (the primary couple and the sceptic say the honest blanks are why they trust the numbers) but trim each to the two or three items that matter for that venue, leading with capacity or exclusive use and curfew. Examples (keep any fact comments that follow): Out of the Blue '- **Not published:** capacity, room count, ceremony types at each setting, exclusive use, curfew.' becomes '- **Not published:** capacity, exclusive use, curfew.'; Caramel '- **Not published:** legal ceremony options, capacity, room count, exclusive use, curfew.' becomes '- **Not published:** capacity, exclusive use, curfew.' (the legal ceremony gap is already covered by the paragraph below it); Elounda Peninsula '- **Not published:** venue capacities, room count, exclusive use, curfew.' becomes '- **Not published:** venue capacities, exclusive use, curfew.' Keep the table and its 'Not published' cells unchanged. Note for cms-publisher: the table must scroll horizontally on mobile, and the existing 'Jump to an area' list stays.

should_fix.issue: The first Concierge link arrives in Key takeaways, before any venue evidence, and with three linked CTAs plus the repeated closers the page reads as selling between sections.
should_fix.fix: Remove 'If you would like a second pair of eyes on the shortlist from the start, [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary).' from below Key takeaways. Place the primary CTA after some venue evidence: under the comparison table (where 'talk to a Wedded Advisor about your shortlist' already sits) or after the house-rules paragraph in 'How to compare Crete venues like for like'. Keep the UTM tags and the quiet 'when you are ready' tone. CRO owns the final wording; use only brand-facts claims.

should_fix.issue: The page reads as Australians only. 'Works in your time zone and quotes in AUD' made a Singapore reader ask whether the service is for her, and a family split between Dubai, London and Sydney felt it was written for someone else.
should_fix.fix: In the closing section only, replace 'Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.' with 'Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples. Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.' (both brand-facts lines). Keep AUD everywhere else, including under the table, and keep 'fly long-haul from Australia', since the brief's reader is Australian. Make no other claims about the service.

consider.issue: The FAQ 'When is the best time to get married in Crete?' answers what time of day, not which months, so it reads as if it dodged the question.
consider.fix: Answer months only as far as the sources go (fact_308, fact_102, fact_205). Replace 'Spring and autumn ceremonies can start earlier in the day. In April, May and October, Nana Princess recommends 4pm to 6pm; in July and August, 6.30pm to 8pm, because of the heat. <!-- fact_102 --> Wildfires occur from June to September. <!-- fact_205 -->' with 'Minos Palace describes the weather in eastern Crete as pleasant from April to November. <!-- fact_308 --> In April, May and October, Nana Princess recommends ceremonies from 4pm to 6pm; in July and August, 6.30pm to 8pm, because of the heat. <!-- fact_102 --> Smartraveller notes wildfires from June to September and frequent heatwaves over summer. <!-- fact_205 -->' Do not name a 'best' month. If that still reads as a dodge, rephrase the question to 'Which months and ceremony times suit a Crete wedding?'

consider.issue: Accessibility for older guests. Only Sea View by En Kipo mentions access (an accessible WC), and it has no rooms; the funding parent does not know whether a walking frame can get from room to chapel at any resort.
consider.fix: Make no access claims about any venue. In 'How to compare Crete venues like for like', after the house-rules paragraph, add one line framed as a question to ask: 'If an older guest or anyone with limited mobility is coming, ask each venue how many steps there are between guest rooms, the ceremony and the reception, and whether there is level access.' Do not add it to the list the Wedded Advisor confirms, and do not add an access column to the table.

consider.issue: The identical line 'Through the shared Elounda Collection packages: civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic.' appears under both Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare, and repeated 'package' wording makes a high-value reader feel slotted into a tier.
consider.fix: The area intro already says the three hotels 'share one weddings team and one set of packages'. Under Porto Elounda, replace '- **Ceremony:** Through the shared Elounda Collection packages: civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic. <!-- fact_302 --> <!-- fact_15 -->' with '- **Ceremony:** Civil, Greek Orthodox or symbolic, through the shared Elounda weddings team. <!-- fact_302 --> <!-- fact_15 -->'. Under Elounda Mare, replace the same line with '- **Ceremony:** The same three options as Porto Elounda. <!-- fact_302 --> <!-- fact_15 -->'. Keep the Ceremony field so every venue has the same fields.

conflicts_resolved: Already fixed in 05-draft-r2.md, so no action: the sceptic's medium trust loss over 'largest' (the Elounda intro now reads 'from banquet spaces for several hundred to an adults-only peninsula', the FAQ east answer no longer claims the largest resorts, and the west paragraph carries the largest-capacity claim backed by Avra's 680), and 'the costliest mistake on Crete' (now 'Booking guests into the wrong airport adds hours to their trip.').

Advisor closer: qa-gates allows the 'confirms in writing' line once per section, but four readers including the primary couple found that frequency a sales loop. The rule is a ceiling, not a requirement; two uses keep the promise without the template feel.

'Not published' lines: search_visitor and funding_parent found them repetitive, while planner_couple (primary) and sceptic said the honest blanks are why they trust the numbers. Keep every line and the table cells, trim each list to what matters.

Public transport (licensed taxis, Chania public bus, coaches per flight wave): uhnw wants private cars, meet-and-greet and private aviation instead. Private transfers are a deferred business detail and nothing may claim the Advisor books transfers, so add no private-logistics copy. The coach-per-flight-wave advice serves the primary couple's 60 to 150 guests and stays.
AUD and Australian framing: search_visitor and uhnw felt excluded, but the brief's reader is an Australian couple. Soften in one place only (the closing section) with brand-facts wording, keep AUD.
Legal section length: uhnw would delegate it to lawyers, while planner_couple (primary) and funding_parent would share it with parents. Keep it and make it easier to read.
Price ballpark: search_visitor wants one, but the house rule is no prices without Nic's sign-off. Print no figure.

Who handles paperwork, who is on the ground, whether the first step is a phone call, fee model, commissions, deposits, contract language, security and full-property closure: raised by funding_parent, planner_couple, sceptic and uhnw. All deferred business details per the orchestrator's ruling; not must-fix and not added to the copy.
Abaton bar names (uhnw bored) versus dated capacity figures (sceptic, search_visitor praised): keep, since capacity by space serves the primary couple's guest count.

checks.check: Weighted scores computed as sum(score x weight)/sum(weights)
checks.note: Weights planner_couple 0.40, funding_parent 0.20, uhnw 0.20, sceptic 0.10, search_visitor 0.10 (sum 1.0). Enquire: 3x.4+3x.2+2x.2+3x.1+1x.1=2.6. Relevance 4.4, trust 3.8, clarity 4.0, premium 3.8.

Only the repeated Advisor closer reached 3+ personas (4). No high severity from the primary persona. The sceptic's medium trust loss ('largest') is already fixed in r2. Money and accountability questions are deferred by instruction.
Weighted enquiry 2.6 < 3.8 and one must-fix, so 'revise'. Not 'stop': the piece meets the brief (relevance 4.4, primary persona relevance 5).
Every 'replace' and 'delete' string was taken from 05-draft-r2.md, not 05-draft.md.

checks.check: No invented facts, no prices, no Wedded Privileges, no legal-paperwork help, no transfer booking claim

open_questions.question: Deferred business details raised by readers: whether the first step is a phone call before anything is booked or paid, who is on the ground on the day, fee model and commissions, deposits and contract language, a real Crete or Greece wedding to link, private transfers, security and full-property closure. Not must-fix, but enquiry likelihood (2.6) will stay well below 3.8 until some are answered.

assumptions: Persona weights are provisional, but no reweighting lifts enquiry to 3.8, since no persona scored above 3.
The G6 threshold cannot be met by copy fixes alone; the writer revises once per qa-gates and the editor re-checks blocking issues only.
